promotionalText: Make room for music. Slow a song down, follow its chords and lyrics, and practice one comfortable phrase at a time.
description:
Musia makes music practice easier to approach, even if keeping time or finding a melody feels difficult.

LISTEN AT YOUR PACE
Explore an original music catalog with English, Japanese and Chinese performances. Slow playback to 0.25x or speed it up to 2x while preserving pitch. Follow timed lyrics, current words and pronunciation readings where available.

ONE PHRASE AT A TIME
Loop a lyric phrase or set your own A and B markers. See the current and next chord, guitar finger placement, reference melody notes and a visual beat pulse. Keyboard playback controls help you stay with your instrument.

START WITH A KNOWN REFERENCE
First Pulse is a built-in synthesized exercise with verified 60 BPM beats and Em/Am chord changes. It works without an internet connection. Begin by listening, tap along, then play the chords.

A NATIVE MAC WORKSPACE
Move between your library, practice, lessons and history using the sidebar. Keep listening while the window is minimized. Practice sessions and preferences stay on your Mac; export your history as JSON whenever you choose.

HONEST ABOUT THE DATA
Automatically analyzed song beats, chords and melody are labeled as estimates or analysis, not guaranteed scores. Tap feedback compares your screen or trackpad taps with reference beats; it does not grade singing or guitar performance, and device/audio latency can affect results.

No account, microphone recording, advertising or subscription is required. Catalog streaming needs an internet connection. This edition focuses on listening and practice, not in-app song generation.
notes:
Native SwiftUI/AVFoundation macOS app, not a WebView or iOS compatibility app. No sign-in, subscription or microphone permission.

1. In Library open First Pulse (On this device). Select Play mode to see Em and Am fingerings. Play, change speed, and choose an Em phrase loop. This synthesized reference works offline.
2. Open a catalog song, such as Aya Chan Hikari Ame, for streaming audio, timed lyrics/readings and analyzed chords. These references are explicitly labeled Analyzed, not verified performance grades.
3. Minimize the window while playing; playback continues. Navigate to History to inspect local sessions or export JSON. Tap mode measures taps only, not instruments.

The sandbox allows outgoing HTTPS for the public catalog/audio and user-selected file access only for history export. It has no incoming server, recording, hidden paid AI generation or private Studio access. Copyright and commercial distribution rights for the catalog were confirmed by the owner. Existing app privacy disclosures cover hosting access logs; the native app contains no advertising/tracking SDK.
